Describe the benchmark in plain language

Source: R/summary.R
summarise_benchmark.Rd

summarise_benchmark() writes a few sentences per model from a result of authenticity_benchmark(): The score and its weakest column, how close each anchored column is to real people, the behaviour features that differ most from real people and in which direction, and the person fit tails. The text follows fixed rules, so it is the same every time and states only values in the table.

Usage

summarise_benchmark(x, n_features = 2)

Arguments

x

a result of authenticity_benchmark().

n_features

how many behaviour features to name per model.

Value

A tibble with model, score, weakest and summary (the text), in the order of the benchmark table. Printing it shows the text.

Details

The anchored values read as follows: 100 is as close as a second sample of real people, 0 is no better than shuffling the real answers within each item, and below 0 is worse than that.

The benchmark compares models and supports decisions about them. It does not show that synthetic data can replace a field test.

See also

authenticity_benchmark()

Examples

h <- hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait %in% c("H", "C"), ]
real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada" & hexaco_llm$attempt <= 2, ]
bm <- authenticity_benchmark(as_synthetic_list(ca), real, h, fit_scales = character(0),
                             n_splits = 5, n_floor = 5)
summarise_benchmark(bm)
